> [!NOTE]
> **What this PR changes:**
>
> - Retitles the guide for 2027 and adds a 17-row at-a-glance comparison table.
> - Adds `faq_schema` and an `itemlist` of 17 vendor URLs to the frontmatter.
> - Updates vendor pricing (Doppler, Infisical, 1Password, Bitwarden, GitGuardian, cloud managers).
> - Adds OpenBao, Kubernetes-native tools (ESO, SOPS, Sealed Secrets), and an AI-agent/NHI section.
> - Rewrites the decision framework and FAQ.
>
> Readers would be misled by stale vendor prices, overstated product capabilities, and dead itemlist links. The fact-check, frontmatter/link sweep, readthrough, and editorial-stance passes all ran.

### ⚠️ Check these before approving

| ID | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| **F12** | [`content/blog/secrets-management-tools-guide/index.md` L92](https://github.com/pulumi/docs/pull/21892/files#diff-17a53d789fd640d692beea2565f9063cfb0cc8e6202d0975ded5792839f6d8caR92) | The ESC docs don't support "20-plus other providers": they list only a handful of other secrets stores. Suggest: "connecting HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager, 1Password, and other providers through a unified interface." |
| **F13** | [`content/blog/secrets-management-tools-guide/index.md` L96](https://github.com/pulumi/docs/pull/21892/files#diff-17a53d789fd640d692beea2565f9063cfb0cc8e6202d0975ded5792839f6d8caR96) | The audit-log field list doesn't match the docs, which list timestamp, user, action, and source IP. Suggest: "ESC provides [audit logging](/docs/esc/administration/audit-logs/) that records the timestamp, user, action, and source IP for each event, supporting compliance programs like SOC 2." |
| **F14** | [`content/blog/secrets-management-tools-guide/index.md` L118](https://github.com/pulumi/docs/pull/21892/files#diff-17a53d789fd640d692beea2565f9063cfb0cc8e6202d0975ded5792839f6d8caR118) | The source says only that HCP Vault Dedicated clusters are charged per hour. The pricing-change story and the "well over $1,000/month" figure are unsupported. Suggest: "HCP Vault Dedicated, the managed offering, is billed per cluster-hour; confirm current numbers directly with HashiCorp before you budget." |
| **F15** | [`content/blog/secrets-management-tools-guide/index.md` L128](https://github.com/pulumi/docs/pull/21892/files#diff-17a53d789fd640d692beea2565f9063cfb0cc8e6202d0975ded5792839f6d8caR128) | CyberArk has renamed Conjur Cloud to "Secrets Manager, SaaS", so calling Conjur Cloud a new offering is stale. Suggest: "CyberArk also offers a managed SaaS edition, now called **Secrets Manager, SaaS** (formerly Conjur Cloud), alongside…". The table row at L73 says "Conjur Cloud" too. |
| **F16** | [`content/blog/secrets-management-tools-guide/index.md` L132](https://github.com/pulumi/docs/pull/21892/files#diff-17a53d789fd640d692beea2565f9063cfb0cc8e6202d0975ded5792839f6d8caR132) | Akeyless's zero-knowledge mode depends on a customer-held key fragment on a customer-run Gateway, so it isn't unconditional. Suggest: "…as SaaS, with an optional zero-knowledge mode (a customer-held key fragment on a customer-run Gateway) so that Akeyless can't read customer secrets." |
| **F17** | [`content/blog/secrets-management-tools-guide/index.md` L174](https://github.com/pulumi/docs/pull/21892/files#diff-17a53d789fd640d692beea2565f9063cfb0cc8e6202d0975ded5792839f6d8caR174) | The 700 figure is stale: the vendor now says "over 800". Suggest replacing "more than 700 credential types" with "more than 800 credential types". |
